summary.title: MinerU-Diffusion: Rethinking Document OCR as Inverse Rendering via Diffusion Decoding

setting_and_object.category: Architecture (diffusion vision-language model for document OCR)

details: Autoregressive document parsers decode structured output token-by-token, causing latency that scales with output length and error propagation on long documents.

Causal left-to-right factorization makes OCR effectively language-prior-conditioned, so models hallucinate text when semantics are disrupted; the authors argue serialization order is an artifact, not intrinsic to the task.

MinerU-Diffusion: a document-OCR VLM that replaces autoregressive decoding with masked discrete-diffusion decoding conditioned on native-resolution visual features, treating OCR as inverse rendering / posterior inference over a structured token sequence.

Block-wise factorization: the output sequence is split into fixed-size blocks that are coarse-grained autoregressive across blocks (causal attention, KV-cache reusable) but bidirectionally diffusion-denoised in parallel within a block, reducing attention cost from O(L^2) to O(B L'^2) and anchoring positions to bound drift.

Two-stage uncertainty-driven curriculum: first broad/diverse OCR data, then fine-tuning on hard cases mined by inference-consistency disagreement across stochastic passes with confidence-based sample weighting.
2.5B total: Qwen2-VL-7B vision encoder, SDAR-1.7B-Chat-b32 block diffusion decoder (block size 32), randomly initialized abstractor; M-RoPE removed relative to MinerU2.5.
Stage-0 modality alignment on LLaVA-Pretrain (adaptor only) then LLaVA-NeXT (full).
~7.5M samples from the MinerU2.5 dataset, Chinese/English document parsing (layout detection on full pages, cropped-region recognition for text/formula/table in OTSL).

Stage-1 (D_base): seq len 12288, batch 256, lr 4e-5, 9 epochs; Stage-2 (D_hard + replay): seq len 16384, lr 2e-5, 4 epochs; visual token budget 2048/image; document augmentation (geometric, background, photometric, degradation).
Dynamic confidence-threshold decoding (default 0.95, temp 1.0, top-p 1.0), block size 32; throughput measured as TPF/TPS on one H200, batch size 1.
OmniDocBench v1.5 (1,355 pages, w/ and w/o GT layout; text edit distance, formula CDM, table TEDS/TEDS-S, reading order), table subsets of CC-OCR and OCRBench v2, formula on UniMER-Test.
Semantic Shuffle: 112 English FOX document images with a controlled proportion of words shuffled and re-rendered with consistent formatting, isolating visual reading from linguistic priors.
Baselines: MinerU2.5, PaddleOCR-VL, dots.ocr, MonkeyOCR-pro, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Gemini-2.5 Pro, GPT-4o, pipeline systems.
Ablations: confidence threshold sweep 0.5-0.99; static (step=6/32) vs dynamic decoding; full-attention diffusion (LLaDA-MoE-7B-A1B) vs block-attention; Stage-1 only / Stage-2 only / both.

key_findings.finding: Diffusion decoding delivers large decoding speedups at accuracy comparable to autoregressive document parsers.
key_findings.evidence: At threshold 0.95 the model reaches 108.9 TPS with 93%+ relative accuracy (2.1x over MinerU2.5's ~52 TPS) and 164.8 TPS at >90% accuracy (~3.2x peak); reported trade-off points include 2.12x speedup at 99.9% and 3.01x at 98.8% relative accuracy. On OmniDocBench v1.5 it scores 93.37 Overall with GT layout (vs 93.44 MinerU2.5, 93.91 PaddleOCR-VL) and 88.94 without.

key_findings.finding: Autoregressive OCR decoders rely heavily on linguistic priors, whereas diffusion decoding stays anchored to the visual signal.
key_findings.evidence: On the Semantic Shuffle benchmark (shuffled and re-rendered FOX pages), AR decoders degrade sharply and monotonically with distortion level while the diffusion decoder's performance remains nearly constant.

key_findings.finding: Block-wise attention is essential for stable, scalable diffusion OCR; full-attention diffusion suffers fixed-length mismatch pathologies.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation with LLaDA-MoE-7B-A1B trained on OCR: full attention costs ~L^2/B token interactions per training step vs ~2L for block attention; qualitative table cases show over-provisioned preset lengths (e.g., L=1024 on a short table) repeat empty rows dozens of times and under-provisioned lengths truncate, while block attention at L=1024 terminates cleanly.

key_findings.finding: Confidence-threshold-based dynamic parallel scheduling dominates fixed-step schedules on both axes.
key_findings.evidence: Dynamic tau=0.97 gives 93.34 Overall at 98.32 TPS versus static step=6 at 88.31 Overall / 91.56 TPS and static step=32 at 93.02 Overall / 21.86 TPS; sweeping threshold 0.5->0.95 raises Overall from 87.61 to 93.37 (table TEDS 81.10 -> 90.99), with a slight decline at 0.99.

key_findings.finding: The two-stage curriculum is necessary: hard-case training alone collapses, while stage ordering pushes past the stage-1 plateau.
key_findings.evidence: Stage-2 only reaches 89.33 Overall with GT layout but only 35.71 without GT layout (reading order 0.472) and shows large gradient oscillation; Stage-1 only saturates at 92.89 / 86.13; the full curriculum attains 93.37 / 88.94 and >89% training accuracy.
